BeforeModelCallEvent는 structured_output 호출에서 발생하지 않습니다' while L435 says this applies only to the deprecated Agent.structured_output() path (API ref: 'not fired for invocations to structured_output'); L742 says handle_request returns result.structured_output via summarize_within_budget, but summarize_within_budget (L674) passes no structured_output_model; same facts restated in several places (see principles.facts_said_once).
score_evidence.D: Hard parts get worked numeric examples (hook nesting table L145, limit overshoot table L644, attempt counting table L420, retry schedule L514). Some over-explanation and repetition push length to ~58K chars.
score_evidence.E: Good tables and code where useful; ASCII diagrams labelled as illustrations. Deductions: llama.cpp row 'llama.cpp | — | —' (L878) where the docs give Python supported / TypeScript not; trivial formulas 'N ≤ 3k' (L283) and 'attempts = n + n' (L395) add little.
score_evidence.F: Two wrong claims in the sample (steering in Python described as an intervention-layer handler, L489; llama.cpp support cells blank, L878). Outside the sample: Cedar's principal_resolver presented as HumanInTheLoop's 'principal' for approvals (L830); 'approval_gate 승인 단계가 바로 이 공식 경로에 해당' conflates middleware interrupt with HumanInTheLoop (L882); 'Guide 재시도에도 프레임워크는 상한을 두지 않으므로' extended from interventions to steering without support (L496).
score_evidence.T1: APIs are real (verified imports/signatures in 1.63.0), but the final handler serve_summary_request (L781-785) never passes structured_output_model, so summary is always None on success (reproduced with a fake model: SummaryReply(outcome='ok', summary=None), no structured-output tool offered). HITL snippet (L820-827) uses HumanInTheLoop without importing it (NameError). handle_request (L405) uses a module-level shared Agent, contradicting the per-request pattern. Middleware snippets L277/L308 use an undefined 'agent'.
score_evidence.T2: Covers all major source topics (loop, hooks, middleware, structured output, interventions, steering, retry, conversation management, limits/cancel, HITL, telemetry/eval) in a sensible order; little padding.
score_evidence.T3: Strong internals: event order and batch vs per-call events, hook-outside-middleware layering, strategy-outside-chain retry stacking, limit check at loop top with overshoot, best-effort proactive compression, token estimator heuristics. Python steering mechanism misdescribed (plugins, not interventions).
